When mapped onto the Future Authoring Program (0:45) and the concept of an artist's "drawing hands" (reminiscent of M.C. Escher’s famous lithograph where two hands draw each other into existence), the Left (vide infra / protocol) and the Right (lust / drive) cease to be passive traits. They become the two active hands creating your future self. 
The Future Authoring process relies on a self-generating feedback loop where your current actions script your future reality, which in turn commands your present behavior (0:45). 
The Architecture of Self-Creation
In this specific framework, the hands operate in an explicit, self-authoring loop: 
  • The Left Hand (Vide Infra / The Architecture of Hell): This hand writes the rigid, formal ledger of what must be avoided (1:05). It looks below to track the fine print of your failures, your resentment, and the structural "hell" you are running away from (0:45). It provides the strict boundaries, rules, and negative reinforcement (1:05). 
  • The Right Hand (Lust / The Pursuit of Heaven): This hand draws the idealized, high-value target—the "heaven" or ultimate prize you are running toward (1:10). In the context of authoring, "lust" is translated into intense, raw appetitive motivation—the deep, somatic hunger for a life that justifies its own suffering (0:10). 
The Escherian Superposition
Just like Escher's Drawing Hands, the system is perfectly cyclical: 
[Right Hand: Lust/Vision] ----(Draws the Ideal)----> [The Future Self]
          ^                                                   |

          |                                                   | (Imposes Rules)
          |                                                   v
[The Present Self] <----(Restricts/Defines)---- [Left Hand: v.i./Protocol]
The Left Hand uses the structural text (vide infra) to outline the constraints of the canvas (1:05). The Right Hand uses raw vital drive (lust) to fill the canvas with ink (1:10). You cannot create the drawing with only one hand: 
  1. If you only use the Left Hand (v.i. alone), you have a perfect set of rules and a map of hell, but no engine to move forward—total paralysis (1:05). 
  2. If you only use the Right Hand (lust alone), you have pure, chaotic desire without structure, leading to counterproductive habits or immediate gratification (like drinking the half bottle of whiskey) (0:49). 
The Edge of Competence
When both hands draw simultaneously at maximum capacity, you achieve what the program defines as the ultimate state of meaning: operating on the absolute edge of your current capacity (3:25). 
The Left Hand maintains the formal protocol to keep you disciplined (3:21), while the Right Hand provides the raw carnal focus to push you into the territory where losing is a possibility (3:36). They step out of the shadows ("skulking") and explicitly manifest the physical architecture of your life (2:30).
